name: Shipping chokepoints
value: Hormuz largely shut; 3 tankers hit 5 Nov
summary: Iran says three tankers hit mines and caught fire in Hormuz on 5 Nov; 35 vessels hit in October
state: Iran's forces said a tanker caught fire after striking a mine in Hormuz on 5 Nov and that three more hit mines, and UKMTO reported a tanker hit by two projectiles north of Qatar late on 4 Nov (Al Jazeera). UKMTO counted 35 vessels hit in October, the most of the war (Nation Thailand). Traffic remains materially impeded, meeting the Alert line.
for_you: Shipping delays and higher freight and insurance costs feed through to energy and goods prices. Mariners should follow UKMTO advisories.

sources.title: Al Jazeera — Iran says tankers struck in Hormuz amid fears of new US attack
Nation Thailand — Iran reports three tankers damaged in Hormuz

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
